correctness.rationale: The exact product law d(yz)/dt=0 proves the full positive-leaf equivalence by uniqueness. Explicit logistic solutions give x=g/(b+k exp(-gt)), y=lambda/(1+h exp(-lambda t)), z=q/y. If g/lambda is positive noninteger and h,k nonzero, x has a nonzero noninteger leading power in s=exp(-lambda t), whereas 1,y,z are analytic integer-power functions; the latter three are independent because y varies and z=q/y. Therefore the single-leaf five-column kernel is exactly span((-q,0,0,0,1)); two different q values kill that kernel. Subtracting the unique first-leaf pairwise fit gives exact off-leaf error theta(q1-q0) and equilibrium displacement theta(q1-q0)/b. The separately packaged standard-library exact-rational script checks ODE differentiation and two explicit nonzero minors. The analytic argument, not finite checks, supports arbitrary admissible parameters.

value.rationale: The primary ecological literature explicitly motivates the inverse problem of whether pairwise interactions can hide genuine hard higher-order terms. This exact model exhibits perfect infinite-time camouflage—not merely good numeric approximation—while proving a sharp, actionable experimental boundary: one nonstationary leaf has exactly one coefficient ambiguity; a second different leaf identifies the whole five-parameter per-capita dictionary. The out-of-leaf prediction discrepancy quantifies the cost of fitting the wrong mechanism. Although a deliberately integrable mechanism, the structural limitation and remedy address an identifiable ecologically meaningful gap rather than an arbitrary numeric slice.
